Traditional antibiotic discovery methods have not kept pace with the rapidly evolving resistance mechanisms of pathogens, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. In this context, antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent a promising class of therapeutics due to their selectivity toward bacteria and slower induction of resistance compared to classical, small molecule antibiotics. However, designing effective AMPs remains challenging because of the vast combinatorial sequence space and the need to balance efficacy with low toxicity. Addressing this issue is of paramount importance for chemists and researchers dedicated to developing next-generation antimicrobial agents.Artificial intelligence (AI) presents a powerful tool to revolutionize AMP discovery. By leveraging AI, we can navigate the immense sequence space more efficiently, identifying peptides with optimal therapeutic properties. This Account explores the emerging application of AI in AMP discovery, focusing on two primary strategies: AMP mining, and AMP generation, as well as the use of discriminative methods as a valuable toolbox.AMP mining involves scanning biological sequences to identify potential AMPs. Discriminative models are then used to predict the activity and toxicity of these peptides. This approach has successfully identified numerous promising candidates, which were subsequently validated experimentally, demonstrating the potential of AI in AMP design and discovery.AMP generation, on the other hand, creates novel peptide sequences by learning from existing data through generative modeling. This class of models optimizes for desired properties, such as increased activity and reduced toxicity, potentially producing synthetic peptides that surpass naturally occurring ones. Despite the risk of generating unrealistic sequences, generative models hold the promise of accelerating the discovery of highly effective and highly novel and diverse AMPs.In this Account, we describe the technical challenges and advancements in these AI-based approaches. We discuss the importance of integrating various data sources and the role of advanced algorithms in refining peptide predictions. Additionally, we highlight the future potential of AI to not only expedite the discovery process but also to uncover peptides with unprecedented properties, paving the way for next-generation antimicrobial therapies.In conclusion, the synergy between AI and AMP discovery opens new frontiers in the fight against AMR. By harnessing the power of AI, we can design novel peptides that are both highly effective and safe, offering hope for a future where AMR is no longer a looming threat. Our paper underscores the transformative potential of AI in drug discovery, advocating for its continued integration into biomedical research.</AbstractText></Abstract><AuthorList However, barriers against IAV transmission remain elusive. We demonstrated human stimulator of interferon genes (STING) as a transmission barrier against IAVs. STING activated nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) and downstream NF-κB-stimulated genes (NSGs) through a specific domain. Among these NSGs, <i>growth arrest and DNA damage-inducible protein 34</i> (<i>GADD34</i>) was crucial for IAV restriction. Some IAVs have evolved to evade activating human STING by mutating residue 115 in their matrix protein 1 (M1), which is essential for efficient viral replication in human respiratory cells. This barrier against the zoonotic threat of IAVs provides a tool for future investigations into the biological functions of the cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monosphosphate (cGMP-AMP) ValidYN="Y">10.1080/19490976.2025.2523811</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising candidates to address the global antimicrobial resistance crisis, yet their traditional design remains labor-intensive and inefficient. Here, we developed BroadAMP-GPT, an integrated computational-experimental framework that combines AI-driven generation, multi-tiered screening, and experimental validation to rapidly discover potent AMPs with broad-spectrum activity. Using this platform, 57% of AI-generated candidates exhibited potent efficacy against ESKAPE pathogens - key culprits of multidrug-resistant infections. An outstanding candidate, AMP_S13, demonstrated exceptional stability under diverse physiological conditions, including extreme pH (2-10), proteolytic exposure, and elevated temperatures, while maintaining minimal cytotoxicity and low hemolytic activity. AMP_S13 also showed robust <i>in vivo</i> efficacy, reducing mortality in <i>Galleria mellonella</i> infection model and accelerating wound healing in a murine MRSA skin infection model. These results validate BroadAMP-GPT as a transformative tool for accelerating the discovery of stable, broad-spectrum and low-toxicity AMPs, offering a scalable strategy to address the urgent threat of multidrug-resistant pathogens.</AbstractText></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author Qualitative variables were analyzed using chi-squared or Fisher&amp;#8217;s exact tests, as appropriate, with R software.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">A total of 206 completed questionnaires were obtained: 123/877 (14%) from &amp;#206;le-de-France, 22/49 (45%) from Mayotte, and 61/162 (38%) from R&amp;#233;union. Reported barriers to vaccination included limited knowledge of their vaccination competence, insufficient promotion and information about the vaccine, and reliance on routine vaccination through general practitioners.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSIONS" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">Midwives have the potential to play a larger role in HPV vaccination. pratiques et attitudes des sages-femmes concernant la vaccination anti-HPV dans diff&amp;#233;rentes r&amp;#233;gions fran&amp;#231;aises. M&amp;#233;thode&amp;#160;: Cette enqu&amp;#234;te transversale descriptive, mobilisant un questionnaire anonyme en ligne, s&amp;#8217;est d&amp;#233;roul&amp;#233;e du 17/10/2022 au 10/02/2023 aupr&amp;#232;s de sages-femmes lib&amp;#233;rales, en r&amp;#233;gion &amp;#206;le-de-France, et dans deux d&amp;#233;partements d&amp;#8217;outre-mer&amp;#160;: Mayotte et La R&amp;#233;union. Le questionnaire &amp;#233;tait structur&amp;#233; en trois parties&amp;#160;: 1) caract&amp;#233;ristiques des professionnels&amp;#160;; 2) pratiques et opinions concernant la vaccination&amp;#160;; 3) freins &amp;#224; la vaccination. Nous avons r&amp;#233;alis&amp;#233; une analyse descriptive et compar&amp;#233; les trois r&amp;#233;gions. Les variables qualitatives ont &amp;#233;t&amp;#233; compar&amp;#233;es &amp;#224; l&amp;#8217;aide du test de chi-deux et du test exact de Fisher selon les conditions d&amp;#8217;application, au moyen du logiciel R. Nos r&amp;#233;sultats montrent que les sages-femmes de La R&amp;#233;union &amp;#233;taient significativement moins favorables &amp;#224; la vaccination anti-HPV (75,4 % versus 89,4 % en r&amp;#233;gion &amp;#206;le-de-France et 86,4 % &amp;#224; Mayotte, p = 0,04), une proportion significativement plus faible de sages-femmes y r&amp;#233;alisaient la vaccination anti-HPV (34,4 % &amp;#224; La R&amp;#233;union versus 64,2 % en r&amp;#233;gion &amp;#206;le-de-France et 54,5 % &amp;#224; Mayotte, p &amp;lt; 0,001). Les freins &amp;#224; la vaccination mentionn&amp;#233;s par les sages-femmes &amp;#233;taient principalement un manque de connaissance de leur comp&amp;#233;tence vaccinale, une insuffisance de promotion et d&amp;#8217;information sur cette vaccination, et le fait de se faire vacciner chez le m&amp;#233;decin g&amp;#233;n&amp;#233;raliste. Complementary to the LPA, it enables a more refined identification of underserved areas and improves the targeting of public policies aimed at reducing territorial inequalities in access to primary care. These findings support broader collection and systematic use of the PNP as a central criterion for analyzing supply&amp;#8211;demand imbalances and as a tool to guide public policy ValidYN="Y">10.3917/spub.262.0119</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText Label="INTRODUCTION" NlmCategory="BACKGROUND">Access to healthcare for migrant and socially vulnerable populations remains marked by significant inequalities. Collective health approaches, defined as interventions bringing together several individuals around shared health issues (information workshops, group discussions, prevention or health promotion activities), are recognized as an important lever for health promotion. However, their implementation among these populations remains challenging. The aim of this study was to explore health perceptions among migrant patients attending a M&amp;#233;decins du Monde center and to identify barriers and facilitators to their participation in collective health activities.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="METHODS">An exploratory qualitative study was conducted at the M&amp;#233;decins du Monde Health and Orientation Centre (CASO) in Nice. Twenty-one exploratory interviews and eight semi-structured interviews were conducted with French-speaking migrant patients until data saturation was reached. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using a thematic approach. Partial double coding was performed using NVivo software.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">Participants displayed contrasting perceptions of health, ranging from a central life priority to a secondary concern behind housing, employment, or administrative regularization. Physicians were perceived positively as central figures of care and protection. Interest in collective activities appeared heterogeneous: Some participants viewed them as an opportunity for sharing, while others expressed reluctance. Several barriers were identified, including language barriers, constraints related to informal work, fatigue, community tensions, and the absence of cultural mediators.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="DISCUSSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">Engaging migrant patients in collective health approaches requires specific conditions, including long-term implementation, co-construction with participants, involvement of peers, and consideration of their life priorities. This exploratory study identifies key feasibility conditions and provides a basis for the design of pilot interventions, whose evaluation and impact indicators will need to be defined at a later stage.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">Collective approaches to health can be a relevant lever for reducing inequalities in access to care, provided they are adapted to the social constraints and life priorities of migrant and socially vulnerable populations.</AbstractText></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author ValidYN="Y"><LastName>Hermet</LastName><ForeName>Laure</ForeName><Initials>L</Initials><AffiliationInfo><Affiliation>Département de santé publique, Centre hospitalier universitaire de Nice, Nice. ValidYN="Y">10.1016/j.celrep.2025.115773</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">S2211-1247(25)00544-3</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Antimicrobial resistance poses a major threat to public health, prompting the development of alternative therapies such as antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). Protein language models (PLMs) have advanced protein structure and function predictions, facilitating AMP discovery. We developed antimicrobial peptide structural evolution miner (AMP-SEMiner), an AI-driven framework that integrates PLMs, structural clustering, and evolutionary analysis to systematically identify AMPs encoded by small open reading frames and AMP-containing proteins in metagenome-assembled genomes. AMP-SEMiner identified over 1.6 million AMP candidates across diverse environments. Experimental validation showed antimicrobial activity in 9 of the 20 tested candidates, with 5 surpassing antibiotic effectiveness; variant peptides derived from these candidates similarly demonstrated strong antimicrobial efficacy. AMPs from human gut microbiomes revealed both conserved and adaptive evolutionary strategies, reflecting their dynamic ecological roles. AMP-SEMiner thus represents a valuable tool for expanding AMP discovery and has significant potential to inform the development of alternative antimicrobial treatments.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright © 2025 The Authors. ValidYN="Y">10.1021/acsptsci.5c00126</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase-1 (NTPDase1, CD39) catalyzes the extracellular hydrolysis of ATP generating AMP, while ecto-5'-nucleotidase (CD73) further hydrolyzes AMP yielding immunosuppressive adenosine. 8-Butylthioadenosine 5'-monophosphate (8-BuS-AMP) was described as a CD39 inhibitor but has been poorly characterized. The standard CD39 antagonist ARL 67156 is not suitable for in vivo studies due to metabolic instability. In the present study, we optimized and upscaled the synthesis of 8-BuS-AMP and performed a comprehensive investigation of its properties. It behaves as a competitive inhibitor at human and mouse CD39, and additionally inhibits CD73. Docking studies using a homology model of human CD39 and determination of an atomic-resolution (1.06 Å) cocrystal structure with human CD73 indicated the inhibitor's interactions within the substrate binding pockets and explained the compound's stability toward hydrolysis. 8-BuS-AMP is metabolically highly stable in human and mouse liver microsomes. It inhibited ε-adenosine formation from ε-ATP and ε-AMP in human synovial fluid and enhanced activation and proliferation of peripheral human T lymphocytes. Thus, 8-BuS-AMP is a recommended tool compound for studying purinergic signaling in vitro and in vivo, being superior to the standard CD39 inhibitor ARL 67156. Moreover, it may serve as a lead structure to develop drugs for the immunotherapy of cancer.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>© 2025 American Chemical
